entry.title: 🚀 Arduino Live System Monitor Using Node.js (jhonny-five)
entry.summary:
Arduino Live System Monitor Using Node.js
A small hobby project that connects Node.js with Arduino UNO R3 to display live system statistics on an I2C LCD module.
The entire project is written in pure JavaScript, using Johnny-Five for serial communication and Standard Firmata on the Arduino side. The goal is to provide a lightweight, hardware-based system monitor that runs independently of any desktop UI. CPU usage (%) Memory usage (%) Download speed (MB/s) Upload speed (MB/s) Automatically detects the active network adapter Live updates via serial communication
Most system monitoring tools are software-based and tied to the operating system UI.
This project explores a different approach by moving system metrics to a physical display, controlled entirely through JavaScript. It also demonstrates: Using JavaScript for hardware control Real-time serial communication with Arduino Practical usage of Johnny-Five beyond basic LEDs and sensors Node.js (>= 18, LTS recommended) Johnny-Five Arduino UNO R3 Standard Firmata I2C LCD Module PCF8574T I2C Controller (configurable) Node.js 18 or higher Arduino UNO R3 with Standard Firmata flashed https://www.instructables.com/Arduino-Installing-Standard-Firmata/
I2C LCD Module PCF8574T I2C Controller (Controller address can be changed in index.js) GPU usage support Temperature and fan speed monitoring Support for other boards (Mega, Nano, ESP32) Configurable refresh intervals Multi-page LCD views Link Contributions and improvements are welcome. Connect the Arduino to your PC via USB Install dependencies and start the app:
bash npm install && node index.js
